items.title: #NoGoodWay Day Campaign Turns Mississauga's Clock Tower Yellow to Retire the R-word
items.summary: According to motionball for Special Olympics, Mississauga's clock tower and city hall will be illuminated yellow on Nov. 18 to mark the national #NoGoodWay Day campaign. The organization says the campaign, running Nov. 4 to Nov. 18, aims to promote inclusive language for people with intellectual disabilities and end the casual use of the R-word. Motionball co-founder Paul Etherington said in a press release that Canadians can use their voices to challenge stereotypes and help build communities where people with intellectual disabilities are treated with respect and dignity. The organization is asking participants to wear yellow, sign an online pledge for inclusive language, and share videos of themselves symbolically destroying the R-word by tearing, deleting or erasing it. Mississauga joins other cities lighting landmarks yellow for the campaign, according to motionball.

items.title: Montcrest Becomes Second Company to Challenge Mississauga's Data Centre Moratorium at Tribunal
items.summary: According to Global News, Mississauga's one year ban on data centre construction is facing a second challenge at the Ontario Land Tribunal, this time from Toronto based real estate investment firm Montcrest Asset Management. The outlet reports Montcrest wants to build a data centre near Eglinton Avenue East and Tahoe Boulevard and is asking the tribunal to exempt its project from the moratorium. This comes as Prologis, an American warehouse developer, is separately challenging the same ban with the tribunal, according to Global News. Mississauga became one of the first Canadian cities to approve a one year data centre moratorium, which took effect in September after a unanimous council vote led in part by councillor turned mayor Alvin Tedjo. Tedjo said ahead of the vote that there were concerns about power consumption, heat islands and noise, Global News reported.

items.title: Reporters Press Tedjo for Specifics on Tax Freeze Savings, Get Few Answers at First Scrum
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo faced repeated questions from reporters on how he intends to pay for the two-year property tax freeze he promised during his campaign. The outlet reports Tedjo spoke to media following the Nov. 16 inauguration of the new city council, reiterating his commitment to affordability without naming which departments or expenditures he would cut. He told reporters efficiencies need to be found but offered few specifics on where those savings would come from, according to The Pointer. Tedjo said the city needs to tighten its own belt before asking residents to do the same, adding that the first budget will show the freeze can be delivered. The outlet notes the tax freeze was the central plank of Tedjo's mayoral campaign, and he said achieving it would require pursuing parallel strategies at City Hall.

items.title: Unprotected Floor Opening at Mississauga Wastewater Plant Led to $100,000 OHSA Fine
items.summary: According to the Ontario Ministry of Labour, the Ontario Clean Water Agency was fined $100,000 after pleading guilty to an Occupational Health and Safety Act offence tied to a workplace fall in Mississauga. The ministry says a worker was critically injured after falling through an unprotected floor opening at a wastewater treatment facility on Nov. 30, 2023. Workers were installing a new motor pump that day, and the job required opening floor hatches at several levels so a crane could lower the motor to a lower subfloor, the ministry said. An electrician and a helper opened the hatches and prepared the area, and a maintenance lead was then told about an issue and told workers to go to lunch, according to the ministry. The agency, which provides water treatment services across Ontario, pleaded guilty in Provincial Offences Court in Mississauga on Sept. 28, the ministry reported.
